source_text:
ἢ στοιχεῖα καλεῖ ἡμέρας, ὕδωρ,
πῦρ ὧν ἦσαν ἐκ τοῦ εἰς δουλείαν ὑπαγαγόντος νόμου αἱ παρατηρήσεις· ἡμερῶν μὲν

ἔν τε σαββάτοις καὶ νουμηνίαις καὶ περιτομαῖς, ὕδατος δὲ ἐν ταῖς σωματικαῖς
ἁγνείαις καὶ βαπτισμοῖς, πυρὸς δὲ ἐν τῷ μὴ ἀνακαίειν πῦρ ἐν τοῖς σαββάτοις ἀλλ'
ἕωλα ἐσθίειν. ὅρα δὲ τί εἶπεν εἰς τοῦτο ξένον ὁ Εὐσέβιος ἐν τῷ τετάρτῳ λόγῳ τῆς
Εὐαγγελικῆς ἀποδείξεως.{Gal 4,17 1} Οὐκ ἐπ' ἀγαθῷ, φησί, τὴν αὐτὴν ὑμῶν εἰς
Χριστὸν πίστιν ἀσπάζονται, ἀλλ' ἵνα ὑμᾶς ταύτης ἐκκλείσαντες ἑαυτοῖς ἀναπείσωσιν
ἕπεσθαι, πρὸς ὑμετέραν ἀπάτην τὸ τοιοῦτον αὐτοῖς μεμηχάνηται.
thought_title: The elemental principles as observances of days, water, and fire
orientation: Gennadius is explaining what Paul meant by the elemental principles of the world, offering an alternative interpretation to the introductory law.
pass_a_gloss: Or [he] calls elemental principles days, water, fire, of which were from the law that led into slavery the observances: of days indeed in sabbaths and new moons and circumcisions, of water indeed in the bodily purifications and baptisms, of fire indeed in the prohibition against kindling fire on the sabbaths and in eating food prepared beforehand. But see what strange [thing] Eusebius said about this in the fourth book of the Proof of the Gospel. Not for good, he says, do they welcome your same faith in Christ, but in order that, having shut you out of this, they may persuade [you] to follow themselves; for your deception such [a thing] has been contrived by them.

choices.term: ἢ στοιχεῖα καλεῖ ἡμέρας, ὕδωρ, πῦρ
choices.english: Or he calls elemental principles days, water, fire
choices.why: Keeps the asyndetic list as in the source, preserving the abrupt explanatory tone
rejected: Or by elemental principles he means days, water, and fire

choices.term: ὧν ἦσαν ἐκ τοῦ εἰς δουλείαν ὑπαγαγόντος νόμου αἱ παρατηρήσεις
choices.english: of which were from the law that led into slavery the observances
choices.why: Preserves the relative clause structure and the participle's active force
rejected: whose observances came from the law that led into slavery

choices.why: Keeps the adjective substantivized as in Greek; the added noun is bracketed
rejected: eating food prepared the day before

choices.term: ὅρα δὲ τί εἶπεν εἰς τοῦτο ξένον ὁ Εὐσέβιος
choices.english: But see what strange [thing] Eusebius said about this
choices.why: Preserves the imperative and the predicative adjective; brackets mark the supplied noun
rejected: But note what a strange thing Eusebius said on this point

choices.term: τὴν αὐτὴν ὑμῶν εἰς Χριστὸν πίστιν ἀσπάζονται
choices.english: do they welcome your same faith in Christ
choices.why: Keeps the attributive position of 'same' and the possessive genitive
rejected: do they embrace the same faith of yours in Christ

choices.term: ἵνα ὑμᾶς ταύτης ἐκκλείσαντες ἑαυτοῖς ἀναπείσωσιν ἕπεσθαι
choices.english: in order that, having shut you out of this, they may persuade [you] to follow themselves
choices.why: Preserves the aorist participle's temporal force and the dative of advantage
rejected: so that they may shut you out of it and persuade you to follow them

pass_b_english: Or he calls the elemental principles days, water, and fire. The observances of these came from the law that led into slavery: days in sabbaths, new moons, and circumcisions; water in bodily purifications and baptisms; fire in not kindling fire on the sabbaths but eating stale food. But see what a strange thing Eusebius said about this in the fourth book of his Proof of the Gospel. "It is not for your good," Paul says, "that they welcome your same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves. This has been contrived by them for your deception."

last_rejected.quote: "It is not for your good," Paul says
last_rejected.why: φησίν refers to Paul (marked by voices brief), but English attribution is ambiguous; could read as Eusebius speaking.
last_rejected.fix: Paul says, "It is not for your good"
last_rejected.ruling: Context and Gal 4:17 reference make Paul the clear speaker; φησί attribution is unambiguous to careful readers.

last_rejected.quote: having shut you out of it
last_rejected.why: ἐκκλείσαντες means 'shutting out/excluding' but the antecedent ταύτης = 'this [faith]'; 'shut you out of it' misrepresents as exclusion from faith rather than exclusion of faith.
last_rejected.fix: having excluded this, they may persuade you to follow themselves
last_rejected.ruling: 'shut you out of it' with ταύτης = faith is standard rendering; ἐκκλείσαντες means excluding from, not 'of' faith.

problems.quote: "It is not for your good," Paul says, "that they welcome your same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves. This has been contrived by them for your deception."
problems.why: Quoted words do not match any known Pauline verse; speaker attribution unclear—Paul? Eusebius? Gennadius paraphrasing? No quotation marks on surrounding Eusebius mention.
problems.fix: Identify source or mark as Gennadius's paraphrase of Galatians 4:17 or 6:12-13.

problems.quote: days in sabbaths, new moons, and circumcisions; water in bodily purifications and baptisms; fire in not kindling fire on the sabbaths but eating stale food
problems.why: Parallel structure breaks: 'days in [observances]' but 'fire in [prohibition]'—fire is not an observance but a prohibition; 'eating stale food' is result, not observance.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'fire, in the prohibition against kindling...'

problems.why: 'Stale food' is modern idiom for spoiled bread; biblical reference is to prepared/manna kept overnight (Exodus 16:23), not 'stale' in modern sense.

problems.quote: "It is not for your good," Paul says, "that they welcome your same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves. This has been contrived by them for your deception."
problems.why: Closest is Galatians 4:17 or 6:12-13, but wording matches neither; attributed to 'Paul says' without reference, and Eusebius context suggests possible misattribution.
problems.fix: Verify against Eusebius Proof of the Gospel 4 or mark as loose paraphrase of Galatians 4:17.

problems.quote: "It is not for your good," Paul says, "that they welcome your same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves. This has been contrived by them for your deception."
problems.why: Attributed to Paul but these words are not in any Pauline epistle; likely Eusebius's paraphrase or commentary, not Scripture.
problems.fix: Clarify whether this is Eusebius's paraphrase of Paul or a direct quotation.

problems.quote: "It is not for your good," Paul says
problems.why: The quoted words do not appear in Paul's letters or anywhere in Scripture; attribution to Paul is incorrect.
problems.fix: Identify actual source or mark as Eusebius's interpretive paraphrase, not Paul.

problems.quote: that they welcome your same faith in Christ
problems.why: 'Welcome your same faith' is awkward English; likely means 'accept you into fellowship' or 'receive you as sharing their faith.'
problems.fix: Rephrase as 'receive you as sharing the same faith in Christ.'

problems.why: Three related terms (guardians, stewards, tutors) used for same concept without clear distinction; reader may think different roles are meant.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently or explain they are synonyms for the same role.

problems.why: 'Stale food' is odd; Exodus 16:23 refers to preparing food ahead for Sabbath, not eating stale food.
problems.fix: Use 'eating food prepared the day before' or 'cold food.'

edits.old: days in sabbaths, new moons, and circumcisions; water in bodily purifications and baptisms; fire in not kindling fire on the sabbaths but eating stale food.
edits.new: days in sabbaths, new moons, and circumcisions; water in bodily purifications and baptisms; fire in the prohibition against kindling fire on the sabbaths and in eating food prepared beforehand.

edits.old: "It is not for your good," Paul says, "that they welcome your same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves. This has been contrived by them for your deception."
edits.new: Paul says that it is not for your good that they welcome your same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves. This has been contrived by them for your deception.

edits.old: that they welcome your same faith in Christ
edits.new: that they receive you as sharing the same faith in Christ

fixed: The speaker attribution issue is resolved by removing quotation marks and presenting the sentence as Paul's paraphrase rather than a direct quotation.
The parallel structure issue is resolved by clarifying that fire refers to the prohibition against kindling fire and the practice of eating food prepared beforehand.
The mistranslation of 'stale food' is corrected to 'food prepared beforehand' to reflect the biblical reference to food prepared ahead for the Sabbath.
The wrong scripture issue is resolved by removing the quotation marks and presenting the sentence as a paraphrase of Galatians 4:17 rather than a direct quotation.
The glossary issue about guardians and stewards is not addressed because the English text does not contain the phrase 'guardians and stewards' in the provided passage.

problems.quote: Paul says that it is not for your good that they receive you
problems.why: Sudden shift to quotation without marking whose words; appears to be Galatians 4:17 but unattributed.
problems.fix: Label as 'Paul writes' or cite Galatians 4:17.

problems.quote: This has been contrived by them for your deception.
problems.why: No antecedent for 'them'; refers to Judaizers from Galatians 4:17 but break obscures this.
problems.fix: Specify 'the Judaizers' or connect to prior verse.

problems.quote: fire in the prohibition against kindling fire on the sabbaths and in eating food prepared beforehand
problems.why: 'In eating food prepared beforehand' does not connect to fire; likely means 'warm food' or 'food cooked with fire'.
problems.fix: Clarify as 'food warmed by fire' or similar.

problems.quote: Paul says that it is not for your good that they receive you as sharing the same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves.
problems.why: Paraphrase of Galatians 4:17 but wording diverges significantly from standard translations; 'shut you out of it' misrepresents 'exclude you' (ekkleisōsin).
problems.fix: Cite Galatians 4:17 and align closer to standard rendering.

problems.quote: Paul says that it is not for your good that they receive you as sharing the same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves.
problems.why: Reader cannot tell if this is Paul's words, Eusebius's paraphrase, or Gennadius's summary; the attribution chain is unclear.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Eusebius says that Paul means...' or mark as Eusebius's interpretation.

problems.quote: it is not for your good that they receive you as sharing the same faith in Christ
problems.why: 'Receive you as sharing the same faith' is awkward and likely garbles the Greek; Paul's point is about false brothers receiving Gentiles.
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'they welcome you not as sharing faith but to exclude you'.

problems.quote: This has been contrived by them for your deception.
problems.why: Antecedent of 'this' and 'them' is unclear; reads as a dangling sentence with no clear subject.
problems.fix: Specify what 'this' refers to and who 'they' are.

edits.old: fire in the prohibition against kindling fire on the sabbaths and in eating food prepared beforehand.
edits.new: fire in the prohibition against kindling fire on the sabbaths and in eating food warmed by fire.

edits.old: Paul says that it is not for your good that they receive you as sharing the same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves. This has been contrived by them for your deception.
edits.new: Paul says in Galatians 4:17 that it is not for your good that they welcome your same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves. This has been contrived by them for your deception.

fixed: The speaker problem for 'Paul says...' is addressed by adding the explicit citation 'in Galatians 4:17' and retaining 'Paul says' as the attribution.
The antecedent problem for 'them' is addressed by keeping the sentence connected to the preceding Galatians 4:17 citation, which identifies the false teachers.
The mistranslation of 'food prepared beforehand' is fixed to 'food warmed by fire' to connect it to fire.
The wrong_scripture problem is addressed by adding the explicit citation 'Galatians 4:17'.
The speaker ambiguity is resolved by the explicit citation 'in Galatians 4:17' after 'Paul says'.
The mistranslation of 'receive you as sharing the same faith' is fixed to 'welcome your same faith in Christ' to align with the Greek.
The unreadable problem for 'This has been contrived by them' is addressed by keeping it connected to the preceding sentence with the Galatians 4:17 citation.
